sections.skill: Explain how to apply for financial aid and the types of federal, state, and school aid

questions.prompt: Kira wants federal grants, work-study, and federal loans for college. What should she do first?

choices.text: Pay a service to apply for aid for her
Apply for a private student loan
Wait for colleges to send aid without applying

questions.intro: The Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) is used for federal grants (such as the Pell Grant), work-study, and federal loans. Many states and colleges use it for their own aid. It is free; never pay to file.
questions.feedback: The FAFSA is free and opens the door to federal, state, and college aid.

misconceptions.A: Applying is free; paid services are unnecessary

sources: Federal Student Aid (FAFSA): The FAFSA is the free application for federal grants, work-study, and loans; it calculates a Student Aid Index (SAI). Never pay to file it. (https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa)

New Jersey Higher Education Student Assistance Authority (HESAA): New Jersey state aid programs, such as the Tuition Aid Grant (TAG), use the FAFSA or the New Jersey Alternative Financial Aid Application. (https://www.hesaa.org/)

questions.prompt: Why should Kira file the FAFSA as early as she can?

choices.text: Filing late adds interest to every grant
Early filers are guaranteed a full scholarship
Some aid is limited and given out early
The FAFSA can be filed only once in a lifetime

questions.correct_answer: Some aid is limited and given out early
questions.intro: The FAFSA is filed for each school year. Some state and school aid runs out, so deadlines and early filing matter. Check each college's and your state's deadline.
questions.feedback: Limited funds go to early filers first; file every year.

questions.prompt: Two students have the same cost of attendance. Student A's Student Aid Index (SAI) is $2,000; Student B's is $15,000. Who shows more financial need?

choices.text: Neither, because the SAI is a credit score

questions.intro: The FAFSA calculates a Student Aid Index (SAI), which replaced the Expected Family Contribution. Colleges figure need as cost of attendance − SAI (and other aid).
questions.feedback: A lower SAI leaves a larger gap between cost and SAI, so Student A shows more need.

misconceptions.A: Reverses the meaning of the SAI
misconceptions.D: Confuses the SAI with a credit score
